# FDG5102

> DO NOT have publicly exposed methods that take pointers, arrays of pointers, or multidimensional arrays as parameters.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.8 Parameter Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5102
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Do not take the pointer or multidimensional array parameter '{0}' in the publicly exposed member '{1}'

Library only: the text is about publicly exposed methods, whose callers outside the library find pointers and multidimensional arrays difficult to use. FDG5102 reports a parameter of an externally visible method, constructor, operator, delegate or indexer whose type is a pointer, a function pointer, an array of either, or a multidimensional array, at any level of a jagged array. The 5.8.5 introduction allows pointers where interoperability requires them, with an alternative (FDG5124): a pointer parameter of a method or constructor that has an overload of the same name without pointer parameters is not reported. Whether interoperability requires the pointer is otherwise not seen. Multidimensional arrays are reported in every member. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, since they take their signature from the member they override or implement. CA1814 is not mapped: it also reports fields and return values and suggests jagged arrays, which the text does not ask. FDG5124 reports pointer members without an alternative. Changing a parameter type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Pointers and multidimensional arrays are relatively difficult to use properly. In almost all cases, APIs can be redesigned to avoid taking these types as parameters.

> **Rico Mariani:** Sometimes people try these sorts of things to squeeze out more performance. But remember that you aren’t helping anyone if it’s fast but nearly impossible to use correctly.
